title: Customer chorus fragmentation and fixes brief
body:
TL;DR: Collated ~42 customer threads (support tickets + account calls) across enterprise and AI-native accounts. Core pattern = fractured behaviors when requests hit mixed model variants + KV cache misses; customers call this "stuttering answers" or "context drop". Short fixes exist (routing policy tweak + fallbacks) that recover ~55–75% of high-severity cases; longer work involves more deterministic KV-prime logic and a small API surface change for explicit cache hints.

Scope & signal sources:
- Tickets: 22 distinct Zendesk threads (severity P1=6, P2=11, P3=5).
- CSM calls: notes from three account reviews (Enterprise X, Y, Z) where latency + incoherent rollouts surfaced.
- Engineering triage: two SRE postmortems referencing cold shard miss patterns.
- Internal reproductions: 5 minimal repros (attached link in linked_artifacts).

Observed themes (ranked):
1) Context drift when traffic toggles between hosted and dedicated models — often after autoscale bursts. Symptoms: partial completions, repeated tokens, sudden drop in answer quality mid-conversation.
2) KV cache priming instability — warm-up heuristics fail for short-lived chat sessions. Customers with high-turnover sessions see token cost increase and quality variance.
3) Fallback misrouting — fallback to smaller quantized variants reduces throughput but sometimes returns incompatible structured outputs (schema mismatch).
4) Poor visibility for customers — they see only latencies and final errors, not cross-model fallbacks or cache hit rates.

Representative customer quotes (condensed):
- "Our chatbots start repeating themselves after about 6 responses; it feels like the model forgot the last messages." — AI start-up (PLG)
- "We saw a 2x token bill for an integration test run; diagnostics showed repeated re-tokenization due to cache misses." — Fintech enterprise
- "Fallback worked but produced different JSON keys; our downstream parser crashed." — Platform team at RetailCo

Quick (low-effort) patches we can ship in 1–2 sprints:
A) Routing policy flag: anxious-fallback-mode=false (defaults off). When enabled for a customer, avoid switching model variants mid-session unless explicit SLO breached. Implementation: config flag + dashboard toggle. Expected impact: reduces misrouting noise; rollouts reversible.
B) Short-term KV warm-up: on cold session detection, pre-issue 1x priming request using a compact prompt (internal). Cheap and reduces first-100-token variance; ops toggleable.
C) Fallback validation layer: sanity-check structured outputs against a lightweight schema before returning to caller; if mismatch, escalate to logs and optionally return graceful error. Cheap guardrail for enterprise parsers.

Medium (mid-effort) proposals (3–6 sprints):
D) Deterministic KV-priming API: new optional header/cache_hint to let callers indicate expected context window or to pin a "session key" on the serving layer. Backwards-compatible and helps reuse KV across short bursts.
E) Model-variant contract testing harness: offline regression harness that runs customer prompts across model variants to flag output shape changes and token inflation. Integrate with Optimize quality monitor.

Risks & unknowns:
- Exposing cache_hint header increases surface area; needs security review. Potential for abuse if session keys are long-lived (data residency concerns).
- Warm-up requests cost tokens; must weigh against savings from avoided re-generation. Could be a net loss in some workloads.
- Deterministic priming may interact with quantization layers in unpredictable ways; model-centred testing required.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
1) Ship routing policy flag prototype + dashboard toggle (owner: Jun Park) — spike by 2028-04-09, rollout to 10 pilot customers by 2028-04-23.
2) Implement fallback validation layer with feature flag (owner: Miguel Soto) — PR by 2028-04-06, test on RetailCo sandbox.
3) Product to draft API sketch for cache_hint header and propose security constraints (owner: Priya Raman) — draft PRD by 2028-04-16.
4) CS to assemble pilot list and one-pager for customers explaining the tradeoffs (owner: Ayesha Khan) — ready 2028-04-12.

Notes-to-self / open questions (for working discussion):
- How invasive is the fallback schema validation for streaming responses? Could block streaming; maybe only fast-fail on full-response path.
- Is there existing telemetry to estimate token cost delta for warm-up? Need quick metric.
- Can we prototype cache_hint as an opaque session id without storing PII? Ops question + retention TTL.

Appendix: short repro summary (examples):
- Repro A: 1 user session toggles between hosted model (gptx-lite) and dedicated-reserved (gptx-small) after autoscale. Result: mid-stream repeated tokens. Root cause: routing change triggered KV reset.
- Repro B: fallback to quantized variant returns snake_case keys vs. camelCase expected — downstream parsers failed.

Attachments & artifacts referenced: Confluence brief (linked), Zendesk thread ids: ZD-1124, ZD-1198, JIRA-CS-4127, GH patch PR-238.

Decision log (proposal):
- Recommend shipping routing flag + fallback validation immediately as low-risk mitigations. Parallel spike on deterministic priming API.
- If early pilots show >50% reduction in P1 tickets for the pilot cohort, prioritize deterministic priming for Q3 engineering cycle.

End of brief.

Editing notes: this doc mixes verbatim CS quotes, engineering triage notes, and product proposals. It's a working artifact — expect iterations after engineering spike and pilot feedback.
